relevance_reason: Most complete behavioral match across all five requirements. Lookup() checks a TTL cache (FreshFor window), coalesces concurrent requests for the same currency pair into a single goroutine via snapshotFlight channels with waiter counting, wraps the loader in a LoadTimeout context for bounded provider calls, and on timeout or loader failure falls back to stale entries within a configurable RetainStaleFor window (returning the stale Quote with Stale=true). The entire module is FX-quote-domain-specific — it operates on Pair (XXX/YYY currency codes) and Quote structs with bid/ask/spread, exactly the RateQuoteService domain. LRU-by-use-count eviction keeps the cache bounded. The only difference from the target is language (Go vs TypeScript), but the behavioral pattern coverage is unmatched.

Same language as target (TypeScript) with near-identical behavioral coverage. resolve() implements a TTL cache with a 5-second default (ttlMs=5000) — exactly matching the requirement. Single-flight is achieved via a flights Map<K, ActiveFlight<V>>: concurrent callers for the same key receive the same running.completion promise and increment a joiners counter, preventing duplicate provider calls. The loader is raced against a setTimeout deadline via Promise.race (timeoutMs default 1000ms), providing bounded provider calls. On any load failure, the method checks for a stale (expired but retained) cached entry and returns it — the JSDoc explicitly states this design: 'A value remains available after its freshness deadline...callers receive that stale value only when the replacement load fails.' The JSDoc also uses 'currency pair' as its running example, confirming domain fit. The diagnostics() method exposes providerSuccessRatio and per-key state (fresh/stale/loading) for observability.

TypeScript implementation structurally very similar to CoalescingWindow but with a distinct design choice: separate ttlMs (freshness window) and staleRetentionMs (how long stale values are retained for fallback). load() checks the values cache for a fresh hit within ttlMs, then checks the pending Map<K, PendingLoad<V>> for an in-flight request — if one exists, it increments waiters and returns the shared promise (single-flight deduplication). The loader is wrapped with an AbortController (passed via signal so the loader can react to cancellation) plus a rejectDeadline Promise raced against the load, both triggered by a setTimeout at timeoutMs — providing bounded, cancellable provider calls. On catch, it falls back to a stale cached value if within staleRetentionMs, incrementing a stale counter. The snapshot() method exposes liveValues, inFlight, sharedWaiters, staleRecoveries, and timeouts counters. Additionally, a standalone modelCachePressure() function simulates cache behavior including stampede detection (3+ concurrent same-key requests), which informs TTL tuning — a pattern directly relevant to the target's 'merge requests for same currency' requirement.
